title: Euclidean GCD
shortDescription: Find the greatest common divisor by repeatedly replacing a pair with its remainder.
intuition: A common divisor of a and b also divides a mod b, so the problem shrinks without changing the answer.
derivation: Because a = qb + r, the common divisors of (a,b) are exactly the common divisors of (b,r). Repeating ends at gcd(g,0)=|g|.

title: Extended GCD
shortDescription: Compute gcd(a,b) together with coefficients x and y satisfying ax + by = gcd(a,b).
intuition: Track how every remainder is formed from the original pair while Euclid reduces the numbers.
derivation: Back-substitution through Euclid's equations expresses the final non-zero remainder as a linear combination of a and b.

title: Binary Exponentiation
shortDescription: Raise a base to a non-negative power using the binary digits of the exponent.
intuition: Each bit says whether the current squared power contributes to the answer.
derivation: Write n in binary. Successive squaring produces a^(1), a^(2), a^(4), and multiplying selected terms reconstructs a^n.

title: Modular Inverse
shortDescription: Find x such that ax ≡ 1 (mod m) using the extended Euclidean algorithm.
intuition: An inverse exists precisely when a and m are coprime.
derivation: Bézout gives ax + my = 1 when gcd(a,m)=1; reducing the equation modulo m leaves ax ≡ 1.

title: Prime Factorization
shortDescription: Decompose an integer into prime powers using trial division.
intuition: After removing every factor up to √n, any remaining value is prime.
derivation: A composite number has at least one factor no larger than its square root. Repeated division records each exponent.

title: Eratosthenes Sieve
shortDescription: Enumerate primes by marking multiples of each discovered prime.
intuition: A composite is eliminated by its smallest prime factor.
derivation: Starting at p² is sufficient because smaller multiples already have a smaller prime factor.

title: Euler Linear Sieve
shortDescription: Generate primes while marking every composite exactly once by its smallest prime factor.
intuition: Stop multiplying when the current prime divides i, preserving a unique representation.
derivation: Every composite x has a unique pair (i,p) in the loop where p is its smallest prime factor and x=i·p.

title: Euler Phi
shortDescription: Count integers in [1,n] that are coprime with n.
intuition: For every distinct prime factor p, remove the one-in-p share divisible by p.
derivation: Inclusion–exclusion over distinct prime divisors yields φ(n)=n∏(1−1/p).

title: Combination C(n,k)
shortDescription: Compute binomial coefficients exactly with a one-dimensional Pascal recurrence.
intuition: Each choice either includes the newest item or it does not.
derivation: Pascal's identity C(n,k)=C(n−1,k−1)+C(n−1,k) leads to an in-place dynamic program updated right-to-left.

title: Chinese Remainder Theorem
shortDescription: Merge congruences, including compatible non-coprime moduli.
intuition: Two modular progressions intersect only when their difference is divisible by the moduli's gcd.
derivation: Solving m₁t ≡ a₂−a₁ (mod m₂) with extended GCD yields a merged residue modulo lcm(m₁,m₂).

title: Breadth-First Search
shortDescription: Traverse a graph layer by layer and find shortest paths in unweighted graphs.
intuition: A queue finishes every vertex at distance d before any at d+1.
derivation: When a vertex is first discovered, every shorter layer has already been processed, so its recorded distance is minimal.

title: Depth-First Search
shortDescription: Traverse a graph by exploring each branch before backtracking.
intuition: A stack remembers the frontier while exploration dives deeply.
derivation: Marking on entry ensures each reachable vertex and edge is processed a bounded number of times.

title: Dijkstra
shortDescription: Find single-source shortest paths in a graph with non-negative edge weights.
intuition: The unsettled vertex with the smallest tentative distance cannot later be improved by a non-negative detour.
derivation: A min-priority queue greedily settles vertices; relaxation maintains the best known upper bound for each distance.

title: Topological Sort
shortDescription: Order a directed acyclic graph so every edge points forward.
intuition: A zero-indegree vertex has no unmet prerequisite and can be emitted next.
derivation: Kahn's algorithm repeatedly removes zero-indegree vertices; emitting fewer than V vertices proves a cycle remains.

title: Disjoint Set Union
shortDescription: Maintain dynamic connectivity with path compression and union by size.
intuition: Represent each component by a root and flatten paths during lookups.
derivation: Union by size limits tree growth; path compression makes repeated finds nearly constant amortized time.
edgeCases: Union within one component is a no-op

title: Fenwick Tree
shortDescription: Support point updates and prefix/range sums in logarithmic time.
intuition: Each tree cell owns a block whose length is its least significant set bit.
derivation: Adding lowbit moves to the next containing block; subtracting lowbit partitions a prefix into disjoint blocks.

title: Segment Tree
shortDescription: Maintain associative range aggregates under point updates.
intuition: A balanced binary tree stores the answer for every recursively divided interval.
derivation: A query decomposes an interval into O(log n) canonical nodes, and an update changes one root-to-leaf path.

title: Binary Search
shortDescription: Locate a target in sorted data by halving the search interval.
intuition: One comparison eliminates half of the remaining candidates.
derivation: The invariant keeps the target, if present, inside [lo,hi]; each iteration strictly shrinks that interval.
edgeCases: Duplicates may return any matching index

title: Merge Sort
shortDescription: Sort by recursively ordering halves and merging them stably.
intuition: Merging two sorted sequences only needs to compare their front elements.
derivation: The recurrence T(n)=2T(n/2)+O(n) has O(log n) levels of O(n) merging work.
edgeCases: Empty and singleton arrays are already sorted
Stable when ties choose the left half

title: Quick Sort
shortDescription: Sort in place by partitioning around pivots.
intuition: After partitioning, the pivot is final and the two sides can be solved independently.
derivation: Balanced partitions yield logarithmic depth and O(n log n) work; consistently extreme pivots cause O(n²).
